This is a BC-wide tax-topic page, not an area page: titled "First-Time Buyer GST Rebate BC (2026) | Save Up to $50,000," it is a single-topic explainer for the federal first-time home buyers' (FTHB) GST/HST rebate as it applies in BC, where only the 5% GST applies.
Streets, schools and getting around GST Rebate in BC

items.t: The page's structure as read: a status banner, "How the Rebate Works" with a savings table, "Who Is Eligible," "Key Dates & Deadlines," "Important Limitations," "How to Claim the Rebate," an "Other First-Time Buyer Programs in BC" section (BC PTT exemption, RRSP Home Buyers' Plan, first-time home buyer's tax credit), and two FAQ blocks (six questions, then four more).

Where the relevant stock concentrates for this page: nowhere geographic — the page's "stock" is new housing only, meaning newly built or substantially renovated homes bought from a builder (including on leased land), owner-built homes on land the buyer owns or leases, and co-operative housing shares for new units; resale homes are expressly excluded, and the page notes resale homes are not subject to GST.
The page's sources as it cites them: CRA's FTHB GST/HST rebate pages and a Department of Finance Canada GST relief backgrounder, linked from the page.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in GST Rebate in BC

items.t: FTHB rebate — amount and thresholds: together with the GST/HST new housing rebate, the FTHB rebate provides 100% of the GST (or the federal part of the HST) on a newly constructed or substantially renovated single unit residential complex or residential condominium unit valued up to $1 million; between $1 million and $1.5 million the rebate is gradually reduced; and no FTHB rebate is available at $1.5 million or more.

Worked example — the page's $1.25 million row, flagged: input $1,250,000 = $62,500 GST, about $25,000 rebate, about $37,500 net on the page's table — but that row depends on the page's "phases out on a straight-line basis" wording (a $1.25 million home qualifying for a 50% rebate, up to $25,000 back), and the straight-line formula itself was not stated on the CRA pages opened: CRA says only that the rebate is "gradually reduced" between $1 million and $1.5 million, so the mechanism is not verified and the $1.25 million row is page copy, not a verified calculation.

GST New Housing Rebate (the pre-existing rebate): generally 36% of the GST (or federal part of the HST) paid on a newly constructed or substantially renovated single unit residential complex or condominium unit, to a maximum rebate of $6,300; for homes with a purchase price or fair market value between $350,000 and $450,000 the rebate is gradually reduced, and no rebate is available at $450,000 or more.

Do not double-count the old rebate: the long-standing new housing rebate alone is worth at most $6,300 — the $50,000 figure exists only because the FTHB rebate tops the combined recovery up to 100% for qualifying first-time buyers.

First-time buyer definition: the individual must be at least 18 years old, be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, and not have lived in a home — in or outside Canada — that they or their spouse or common-law partner owned or jointly owned as a primary place of residence at any time in the calendar year of the purchase or in the preceding four calendar years.

Property and timing conditions: the buyer must meet the existing new housing rebate's eligibility criteria (or would meet them if that rebate's ceiling were $1.5 million instead of $450,000); must have entered a purchase and sale agreement with a builder on or after March 20, 2025 and before 2031 (for an owner-built home, construction must begin on or after March 20, 2025 and before 2031); construction must begin before 2031 and be substantially completed before 2036; the buyer must be the first to occupy the home as a place of residence after substantial completion; and the buyer must not have previously applied for an FTHB rebate.

Claiming: the application time limit is usually within two years of taking ownership or finishing construction; a builder can credit the rebate against the amount payable when ownership transfers; where the builder does not credit it, the buyer applies directly to the CRA through a CRA account or by mailing Form GST190 (houses purchased from a builder), and an owner-builder who started construction on or after March 20, 2025 applies directly using Form GST191.

First-time home buyer's tax credit as the page states it: a $10,000 non-refundable credit providing up to $1,500 in tax relief — recorded as page copy only, because the credit's amount was not re-read on a CRA page opened pass: Not verified.

blocks.text: Good to know about GST Rebate in BC

items.t: The Royal Assent date on this page is the corrected one — March 13, 2026, not March 12.

The page's PTT paragraph checks out — including its "up to $8,000" saving. The research pass verified the page's PTT wording against the Province page in substance (exemption on the first $500,000 up to the $835,000 threshold, phasing out completely at $860,000), and the "up to $8,000" saving is the general-rate tax on $500,000 — $2,000 at 1% plus $6,000 at 2% — under the verified general rates.

A co-op share can qualify for this rebate even though it is not a condo. CRA News No. 122 states the FTHB rebate is also generally available on a share in a co-operative housing corporation entitling the buyer to occupy a new unit, and on a new home bought on land leased from the builder — two tenure forms a buyer could easily assume are excluded.

The buyer must be the first person to live in the home. Among the verified conditions: the buyer must be the first to occupy the home as a place of residence after substantial completion, and must not have previously applied for an FTHB rebate — a new home that someone else occupied first is outside the rebate on the conditions as read.

The deadline stack has three different clocks. As the page presents it and the CRA conditions confirm in substance: agreements on or after March 20, 2025 and before 2031; construction begun before 2031 and substantially completed before 2036; and an application usually within two years of taking ownership or finishing construction — missing any one of the three ends the claim independently of the others.

items.t: This is a topic page, not an area: titled "First-Time Buyer GST Rebate BC (2026) | Save Up to $50,000," it serves first-time buyers of new homes anywhere in BC, where only the 5% GST applies.

Page structure as read: a status banner, "How the Rebate Works" with a savings table, "Who Is Eligible," "Key Dates & Deadlines," "Important Limitations," "How to Claim the Rebate," an "Other First-Time Buyer Programs in BC" section (BC PTT exemption, RRSP Home Buyers' Plan, first-time home buyer's tax credit), and two FAQ blocks.

This BC-wide topic page has no SnapStats row of its own; SnapStats covers exactly 14 communities with Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined only and community medians only, and land has NO SnapStats category. A market figure for this page is not verified / not applicable.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in GST Rebate in BC

items.t: FTHB GST/HST rebate — verified (CRA News No. 122 + CRA tax-tips page, opened pass): amendments in Bill C-4; Royal Assent March 13, 2026 (CRA governs). Together with the new housing rebate, it provides 100% of the GST (or federal part of HST) on a newly constructed or substantially renovated single unit residential complex or condominium unit valued up to $1 million; between $1 million and $1.5 million the rebate is gradually reduced; no rebate at $1.5 million or more. Maximum $50,000.

FTHB eligibility — verified: at least 18, Canadian citizen or permanent resident, and not have lived in a home — in or outside Canada — that they or their spouse/common-law partner owned as a primary residence in the purchase year or the preceding four calendar years; must meet the new housing rebate criteria (as if its ceiling were $1.5M instead of $450,000); agreement with a builder on or after March 20, 2025 and before 2031 (owner-built: construction begins in that window); construction begins before 2031 and is substantially completed before 2036; buyer is first to occupy after substantial completion; buyer has not previously applied for an FTHB rebate. It also generally covers a home on land leased from the builder and a co-op share for a new unit.

Claiming — verified: usually within two years of taking ownership or finishing construction; a builder can credit the rebate at transfer; otherwise the buyer applies to CRA directly (CRA account or Form GST190 for a builder purchase; Form GST191 for owner-built).

Page statements only — not verified: (a) the straight-line phase-out mechanism and its $1.25M / 50% / $25,000 example; (b) the spousal already-claimed bar; (c) the assignment-sales rule that the original agreement must date from on or after March 20, 2025. None was stated on the CRA pages opened pass.

PTT — general tiers (Province, verified): 1% to $200,000, 2% to $2,000,000, 3% above, plus a further 2% on the residential portion over $3,000,000, on fair market value at registration. Worked anchors: $500K → $8,000; $700K → $12,000; $1.0M → $18,000; $2.0M → $38,000.

BC FTHB PTT exemption — verified: exempt on the first $500,000 where fair market value is $835,000 or less (effective Apr 1, 2024), property 0.5 ha or smaller, principal-residence use only, with the citizenship/residence and never-owned conditions the Province lists; partial exemption $835,000–$860,000. The page's "up to $8,000" saving is the general-rate tax on $500,000.

faq.a: Up to $50,000: together with the new housing rebate, the FTHB GST/HST rebate returns 100% of the GST on a new or substantially renovated home (including a residential condominium unit) valued up to $1 million, is gradually reduced between $1 million and $1.5 million, and is not available at $1.5 million or more.
faq.q: How much GST can a first-time buyer in BC get back on a new condo?

faq.a: On the verified conditions, no: eligibility turns on a builder agreement entered into on or after March 20, 2025 and before 2031, with construction begun before 2031 and substantially completed before 2036 — the signing date is checked before the price.
faq.q: My presale was signed before March 20, 2025 — do I still qualify?

faq.a: Inputs: price $750,000, GST rate 5% — GST payable $37,500; the home is valued at or under $1 million, so the combined FTHB + new housing rebate returns 100% of the GST, $37,500, for $0 net GST, assuming every buyer and timing condition is met.
faq.q: Show me the math on a $750,000 new condo.

faq.a: Bill C-4 received Royal Assent on March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122 — not March 12, as some secondary sources say.
faq.q: When did the rebate become law?

faq.a: It still exists on its own terms: 36% of the GST, maximum $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000.
faq.q: What happened to the old new housing rebate?

faq.a: Yes — separate federal and provincial programs.
faq.q: Can I stack the GST rebate with BC's PTT exemption?

faq.a: No. The FTHB rebate is for new HOUSING — a newly built or substantially renovated home — not bare land.
faq.q: Does the $50,000 GST rebate apply if I just buy a vacant lot?

faq.a: An individual who is at least 18, is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, and has not lived in a home that they or their spouse or common-law partner owned or jointly owned as a primary place of residence in the calendar year of purchase or in the preceding four calendar years.
faq.q: Who counts as a first-time home buyer for this rebate?

faq.a: It still exists on its own terms: generally 36% of the GST paid, to a maximum of $6,300, gradually reduced for homes priced or valued between $350,000 and $450,000, and unavailable at $450,000 or more — the FTHB rebate is the separate top-up that takes a qualifying first-time buyer's combined recovery to 100%.
faq.q: What happened to the old GST new housing rebate?

faq.a: Yes — they are separate federal and provincial programs: the BC first-time program exempts PTT on the first $500,000 of the purchase price where the fair market value is $835,000 or less, with a partial exemption between $835,000 and $860,000, and nothing in either program's conditions as read in this pass bars claiming both.
